--------
In this VladTV interview, John Franzese Jr. reflects on the years after his father returned to prison in 1982 and how his life spiraled from alcohol abuse into cocaine addiction in his early 20s. He describes first trying coke after being told he looked “a mess,” believing it helped him control his drinking—until it took over his life through 2001. As brother Michael Franzese was making millions in the gasoline tax scheme and facing major federal racketeering cases brought during the Giuliani era, John says he stayed close to Michael and their father while avoiding charges. The conversation covers CMC, fuel taxes, union funds, extortion allegations, Florida legal trouble, Michael’s 1986 guilty plea, and the Norby Walters case. John also opens up about becoming intermittently homeless by 1990, bouncing between street life and business meetings at places like Sony.

--------
Marlow Bates sits down with Vlad to revisit his Baltimore murder case, alleging paid-off witnesses, ignored evidence, and a justice system shaped by drugs, politics, and police misconduct. Bates discusses his brother Tony “Cat Eye” refusing a deal to testify against him, questions surrounding witness testimony, and the role of forensic ballistics expert Joseph Chaparro, later accused of using forged credentials. He also compares his case to other claims of wrongful conviction and says he never received a proper court hearing despite years of petitions.

The conversation shifts to prison life, where Bates describes violence, underground economies, inmate “stores,” drug dealing, and the harsh rules that governed survival behind bars. He addresses prison rape, saying he intervened to stop assaults, and explains the dangerous contradiction of inmates engaging in sexual acts while reacting violently to being called gay.

--------
Tito “TJ” Dominguez sits down with Vlad to revisit the chaos surrounding his 1988 arrest, denied bond, and alleged ties to Pablo Escobar’s drug operations as Colombia descended into violence. The conversation covers Escobar’s assassination of presidential candidate Luis Carlos Galán, the attempted targeting of César Gaviria, and the bombing of Avianca Flight 203 in 1989, which killed 107 people, including two Americans, and cemented Escobar’s reputation as a terrorist. Dominguez says he was not involved in the killings and does not condone violence, while recalling firsthand memories of bombings, bodies in Medellín, and a Colombia gripped by fear. He also describes encounters connected to Panama, Manuel Noriega, and the deadly environment around Escobar’s network as the cartel war spiraled out of control. A stark look at organized crime, terrorism, and survival during one of Latin America’s most violent eras.

--------
Terrance “Gangsta” Williams joins VladTV to break down Lil Durk’s not-guilty verdict and what it could mean ahead of the separate VICAR case, short for Violent Crimes in Aid of Racketeering. Drawing on his own prison experience, Williams explains why co-defendant testimony and plea deals often make federal cases difficult to beat, while Vlad discusses reasonable doubt, the role of attorneys Drew Findling and Christy O’Connor, and the broader racketeering allegations still ahead.

The conversation also touches on the Quando Rondo and Lul Tim side of the case, fan reactions to “Free Durk,” and Trap Lore Ross covering the courtroom proceedings. Later, Vlad and Williams discuss reports about an Apple Watch incident in custody before Williams reflects on USP McCreary, contraband, Suboxone, and the harsh realities of prison hustling. A grounded look at hip-hop, federal court, and street consequences.
